ai.description: *Microhyla sholigari* is a tiny frog (16–18 mm) with a brown dorsum and a distinct dark, hour-glass-shaped marking. It features a pointed snout and lacks webbing on its toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Microhyla sholigari* is best distinguished by the distinct, dark, diamond-shaped or "X" marking on its back, which is absent in most other similar Indian *Microhyla* species.
ai.habitat: *Microhyla sholigari* inhabits the leaf litter of moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 700 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sholiga Narrow-mouthed Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging from leaf litter during the monsoon to forage for small invertebrates in moist forest floor habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Microhyla sholigari* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in temporary pools. They exhibit explosive breeding behavior typical of the genus.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Microhyla sholigari* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Sholiga Narrow-mouthed Frog produces a high-pitched, insect-like trill consisting of rapid, rhythmic pulses, typically heard near temporary rain pools in forest habitats.
